title: Get your phone number off people-search sites to cut spam calls
summary: A bot finds where your phone number is listed on people-search and data-broker sites, files the opt-out requests, and checks again later.
what_the_bot_does: Searches people-search and data-broker sites for your name and phone number.
Submits each site's opt-out form using only the details it needs.
Clicks the confirmation links those sites email you.
Re-checks on a schedule you choose, because listings can come back.
what_you_end_up_with: A list of where your number was listed, opt-outs filed, and a regular re-check.

tools.note: The shared example is a Grok Bot template

prompt: Find where my name and phone number [name, city, phone] are listed on people-search and data-broker sites. Make me a list with links. Then submit each site's official opt-out request using only the minimum details it asks for, and confirm any verification emails. Don't pay for any removal service or create accounts without asking me. Re-check every [month] and tell me what's new.
watch_out: Some opt-out pages ask for more personal info than they had. Share only the minimum.
Listings can reappear, so the re-check matters.
This cuts spam calls that come from your number being sold, but won't stop every robocall.

sources.label: X post by @PixelRainbowNFT (2026-10-19): a roundup of Grok Bot templates, including a Spam-Call Scrubber that files people-search opt-outs and re-checks
